Raghav Sharma, Ld. JMFC-06, South East District, Saket Courts, Delhi in complaint case No.
3794/2024 PS Kalkaji titled as "Kanika Gautam Vs Siddharth Chugh & Ors "
whereby Ld.

sentences.text:
JMFC has allowed the application of the complainant u/s.156(3) Cr.PC and directed to register FIR against the revisionist and directed to file compliance on next date i.e. 11.09.2024.
2.

By filing the present revision petition, revisionist seeks to set aside and quash the impugned order on the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C dated 10.09.2024 passed by the Ld. Trial Court whereby direction to register FIR was given.

3. For the sake of brevity, the facts of the case are not repeated here as same has been succinctly mentioned in the order dated 10.09.2024, against which present revision petition is filed and order dated 10.09.2024 be read as part and parcel of the present order.

4. In reply filed by the respondent it is mentioned that the aforesaid order directing the SHO PS Kalkaji to register FIR was passed on 10.09.2024 and in compliance FIR No. 410/24 u/s. 420 IPC PS Kalkaji was registered on 10.09.2024 and compliance report was filed before the Ld. Trial Court on 11.09.2024 in the morning itself.

By the time the above-mentioned revision petition was filed by the petitioner on 11.09.2024, the FIR in compliance of order dated 10.09.2024 was already registered by PS Kalkaji and the compliance report was filed on 11.09.2024.
Thus, the registration of FIR was well within the knowledge of the petitioner before filing of the above- mentioned revision petition.

5. It is submitted by counsel for respondent that once the FIR has been registered by PS Kalkaji in compliance of order dated 10.09.2024, it was incumbent upon the petitioner to mention about the registration of FIR by PS Kalkaji in the revision petition.
However, the petitioner very cleverly did not mention about the registration of FIR in the present revisioin petition and by misleading the court obtained the ex parte stay order dated 12.09.2024.

sentences.text: During arguments, counsel for the respondent submitted that it is no longer res integra that revision petition against the order passed u/s. 156(3) Cr.PC for directing registration of FIR is maintainable but same is maintainable before the registration of FIR by the SHO in compliance of the order and not after the registration of FIR, as, after the registration of FIR only Hon'ble High Court has power to quash the FIR and Sessions Court has no power to quash the FIR.
On the other hand, counsel for the revisionist submits that revision petition even after registration of FIR is maintainable.
7. Both counsels have filed judgments in support of their arguments.

8. Court will first decide the legal objection taken by Counsel for respon- dent to the maintainability of the revision petition on the ground that FIR No. 410/24 u/s. 420 IPC PS Kalkaji in compliance of impugned order dated 10.09.2024 was already registered before filing of revision petition and there- fore, present petition is not maintainable.
9.

Neither of the counsel could file any authority on the abovementioned point passed by either Hon'ble High Court of Delhi or Hon'ble Supreme Court of India but counsel for the revisionist has relied upon the order passed in Writ Petition No. 2517/2022 titled "Arun P. Gidh Vs.
Chandraprakash Singh and Ors", wherein reference was made by Ld. Single Judge of Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay to larger Bench of three Judges of the same court regarding "Whether remedy of revision under Section 397 of the Cr.PC, is available to the person agrrieved by an order directing investigation, to be made pursuant to an order passed under Section 156(3) of Cr.PC.?"
10.

entities.text:
Arun P. Gidh Vs.
Chandraprakash Singh and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Three Judge Bench in the reference petition framed two questions which are mentioned at para 45 :
"(i) Whether a revision u/s. 397 of the Code is an efficacious remedy against an order directing investigation u/s. 156(3) of the Code passed by the Magistrate even after it results in registration of the FIR and further proceedings pursuant to such investigation ?

(ii) To what extent the revisional court can interfere with the subsequent actions and proceedings in the investigation after registration of the FIR pursuant to a direction under Section 156(3) of the Code ?
11.

After discussing the relevant law on the reference point, the Hon'ble High Court in Para 126, 127 and 128 gave the conclusion of their discussion which are reproduced herein below:-
"Para 126.

( a ) If the FIR is yet not registered, an interim order passed by the revisional court,
staying effect and operation of the impugned order under Section 156(3), will have full play and the investigating agency cannot proceed to register the FIR and enter Siddharth Chugh vs State Of Nct Delhi on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126506296/
2 into investigation lest the order passed by the revisional court would be denuded of the meaning and content.

entities.text: Siddharth Chugh vs State Of Nct Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (b) Such in interim order before the registration of the FIR will operate with full force and vigor, irrespective of the nature of the infirmity in the impugned order which weighed with teh revisional court to stay such an order.
(c) On the other hand, if the FIR has already been registered, before the revisional court passes an interim order, then the nature of the infirmity in the impugned order may become relevant.

(d) If the revisional court finds that the impugned order suffers from jurisdicational error, (of the nature referred to in Pra nos.119,120 and 122 above), in our considered view, the revisional court must be construed to have the power to stay further proceedings pursuant to the registration of hte FIR if the matter is still at the state of investigation.

(e) We hasten to add that while passing such an order of stay of the proceedings at the stage of investigation, the revisional Court ought to record reasons which weighed with the court to hold that there appears a jurisdictional error in passing an order under Section 156(3) of the Code and thereupon, in terms, direct that the further proceedings be stayed.
(f) However, where the investigation culminates into lodging of the chargesheet and/or cognizance has been taken by the jurisdictional court, the interim order or final order passed by the revisional court setting aside the order passed by the Magistrate under Section 156(3), will not have the effect of quashing the resultant prosecution.
Para 127.

We are unable to persuade ourselves to agree with the submission of Mr. Desai that the view that after FIR is registered revision is not an efficacious remedy, would render the statutory remedy of revision redundant.
The order passed by the revisional court setting aside a direction for investigation, even after registration of FIR, cannot be said to be bereft of any utility.
If such an order is passed before the completion of investigation, the investigating agency may take the same into account in determining the course the investigation shall culminate into.

If such an order is passed, post loding of the chargesheet, the jurisdictional Magistrate may have the benefit of the said order at the stage of taking cognizance or during the course of the inquiry, as envisaged by the Code.
The High Court may also have due regard to the order of the revisional Court while considering the prayer for quashing the FIR and / or prosecution in exercise of writ or inherent jurisdiction.
Para 128.

The conspectus of aforesaid discussion is that in our view, the decision of the Division Bench in the case of Kailash Dattatraya Jadhav (supra), that in a case where on the basis of an order under sub-Section (3) of Section 156 of the Code, FIR is registered, the remedy of revision under the Code, is not an efficacious remedy, lays down the correct position in law."

sentences.text: After concluding it discussion, Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay gave the answers to the questions framed in para 45 which is reproduced herein below :-

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: "Para 129.
We are, therefore, inclined to answer question (i) in the negative.
As regards question (ii) in our view, the revisional Court can interfere with an order under Section 156(3) at the stage and to the extent indicated in para 126."

13. So, as per the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay the revision petition is not an efficacious remedy against an order under Section 156(3) for registration of FIR, if, FIR got registered; revisional court can only interefere if order suffers from jurisdictional errors like non filing of supportive affidavit along-with application u/s. 156(3) Cr.PC as ordained by "Priyanka Srivastav & Ors. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & ors.", (2015) 6 SCC 287, or lack of previous sanction as required before registration of FIR or in case of medical negligence where prior opinion from independent and competent doctor in Govt. Service not obtained; facts of the present complaint shows that there is no such jurisdictional error in the present case.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastav & Ors. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & ors.", (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Once an FIR has been registered only Hon'ble High Court has power to quash it u/s. 528 BNSS (482 Cr.PC) and Sessions Court has no power to quash the FIR or stop the investigation or interefere in the investigation.

What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly; once an FIR has been registered no revision petition against the same is maintainable as in case revision petition is allowed and order directing registration of FIR is set aside it will tantamount to quashing of FIR.
15. In view of the above discussion, present revision petition is hereby dismissed.
The stay granted vide order dated 12.09.2024 is hereby set aside.
16. Copy of this order be sent to Ld. Trial Court alongwith TCR.
17. File of revision petition be consigned to Record Room after due compliance.
